traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements for 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS are implemented and verified:
- **Optional Warning (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING)**: `processComment` emits `preferImplements` diagnostics when both `@story` and `@req` are present and no `@supports` exists. Tests explicitly assert this behavior. - **Auto-fix Support (REQ-AUTO-FIX)**: `buildImplementsAutoFix` and `applyImplementsReplacement` construct a `@supports` line and remove the original `@story`/`@req` lines. Jest tests validate the exact transformed output for single `@req` and multiple `@req` cases. - **Single Story Conversion (REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX)**: Auto-fix only activates when exactly one `@story` path and at least one simple `@req` line are present; the resulting `@supports` line includes all requirement IDs. Covered by the `[REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX]` test. - **Multi-story Detection (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT)**: `analyzeComment` and `hasMultipleStories` detect multiple distinct story paths; `processComment` reports `multiStoryDetected`. Mixed legacy and `@supports` usage reports `cannotAutoFix` with a detailed reason. Both scenarios are tested. - **Preserve Order / Format (REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT)**: The fixer replaces the original `@story` line in-place (`storyIdx`) and removes only `@story`/`@req` lines, preserving the relative position of other comment content (e.g., description, `@param`). It also reuses the original leading whitespace/`*` prefix for consistent formatting. - **Configurable Enforcement & Default Off (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY)**: The rule’s `meta.docs.recommended: false` and absence from `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` ensure it is not enabled in `recommended` or `strict` presets. Tests confirm it’s missing from those configs and can be set to `"warn"` or `"error"` in flat configs. - **Both Formats Valid (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION)**: Valid-case tests show that comments with only `@story`, only `@req`, only `@supports`, or certain mixed non-migration patterns are ignored by this rule. Core validation rules (`valid-annotation-format`, `valid-req-reference`, etc.) remain unchanged; this rule only adds recommendations when enabled. - **Valid Output (REQ-VALID-OUTPUT)**: Auto-fix is conservative: it bails out when `@story` or `@req` lines are complex or ambiguous (sets `storyPath` to null), and therefore only produces `@supports` lines that conform to the known format (path + one or more IDs). Tests for “complex” annotations assert that the rule warns but does not apply a fix. - **Documentation**: `docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md` and `user-docs/migration-guide.md` document the rule, its configuration (off/warn/error), and show before/after auto-fix examples, satisfying the documentation acceptance criterion.
Given the implemented rule, comprehensive tests tied explicitly to this story, passing test suite, and detailed documentation, the story is fully implemented.
